record.paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
record.original_question: For symmetric random band matrices whose bandwidth W ranges from 1 to N-1 in dimension N, determine the transition from Poisson bulk eigenvalue statistics to Gaudin-Mehta statistics and locate the sharp threshold. The conjecture highlighted in the source predicts a narrow transition region around W≈√N.

evidence.quote: As the bandwidth W increases from 1 to N - 1 = dim(M) - 1, the eigenvalue statistics must change from Poisson to Gaudin-Mehta. A back of the envelope calculation suggests that there should be a (sharp) transition in a narrow region around W ≈ √N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N \geq 2$ and $1 \leq W \leq N-1$ be integers. Consider the ensemble of real symmetric $N \times N$ random band matrices $H = (H_{ij})_{1 \leq i,j \leq N}$ defined by:
- $H_{ij} = H_{ji}$ are independent (up to symmetry) centered random variables with finite variance,
- $\mathbb{E}[H_{ij}^2] > 0$ if $|i-j| \leq W$ (with indices taken either on the line or on the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$), and $H_{ij} = 0$ if $|i-j| > W$,
- the nonzero variances are normalized so that $\sum_{j} \mathbb{E}[H_{ij}^2]$ is independent of $i$ (typically of order $1$).

For an energy $E$ in the bulk of the limiting spectrum, let $\{\lambda_k\}$ denote the eigenvalues of $H$ and consider the local statistics of the rescaled point process $\{N \rho(E)(\lambda_k - E)\}$, where $\rho(E)$ is the limiting density of states at $E$.

It is expected that as $W$ grows from $1$ to $N-1$, the local bulk eigenvalue statistics undergo a transition from a Poisson point process (associated with localized eigenvectors) to the Gaudin–Mehta sine-kernel statistics of the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (associated with delocalized eigenvectors). 

Prove that this transition is sharp and locate the critical bandwidth. Specifically, establish the conjecture that there exists a critical scale $W_c(N) \asymp \sqrt{N}$ such that:
(i) if $W \ll \sqrt{N}$, the local bulk eigenvalue statistics converge to a Poisson point process and the bulk eigenvectors are localized;
(ii) if $W \gg \sqrt{N}$, the local bulk eigenvalue statistics converge to the Gaudin–Mehta (GOE sine-kernel) process and the bulk eigenvectors are delocalized;
and characterize the behavior of the statistics in the transition window around $W \approx \sqrt{N}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture remains open in its sharp form. Substantial progress has been achieved on both sides but neither side reaches the conjectured threshold $W \asymp \sqrt{N}$ in dimension one. Bourgade–Yang–Yau–Yin and subsequent work proved bulk GOE/GUE universality and delocalization for one-dimensional band matrices for $W \geq N^{3/4+\varepsilon}$, with stronger results in higher dimensions. On the localization side, results establish Poisson statistics and localization only for $W \leq N^{1/8}$ (Schenker) and improvements thereof, well below $\sqrt{N}$. The narrow transition window at $W \approx \sqrt{N}$ has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Random band matrices (Bourgade ICM survey)
status_evidence.snippet: The localization-delocalization transition is conjectured at W ~ sqrt(N) in dimension one, with corresponding Poisson-to-GOE transition of eigenvalue statistics; progress to date does not reach this threshold.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture remains open at the critical scale sqrt(N).

status_evidence.title: Bulk universality and quantum unique ergodicity for random band matrices in high dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Bulk eigenvalue universality is proved for Hermitian random band matrices in dimensions d>=7 under W >> L^{95/(d+95)}.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on delocalized side in high dimensions, not at sqrt(N) in 1D.

status_evidence.title: Random band matrices in the delocalized phase, I
status_evidence.snippet: For 1D band matrices with W >= N^{3/4+epsilon}, bulk eigenvalues converge to GOE sine-kernel and eigenvectors are delocalized.
status_evidence.claim: Delocalized side known down to W >= N^{3/4+epsilon}, above sqrt(N).

status_evidence.title: Localization of One-Dimensional Random Band Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Recent works improve the localization regime for 1D random band matrices, but do not reach W ~ sqrt(N).
status_evidence.claim: Localized side improved but does not meet the conjectured threshold.
